item.title: Tokematic 1.1.1370
item.description:
• Claude accounts stay unified: command-line snapshots fold cleanly into active web sessions, preventing duplicate rows and false degradation notices while preserving billing alerts.
  • Clearer quota countdowns: resets over 24 hours show plainly in hours, and quota alerts skip comfortable windows to chime only when a limit approaches.
  • On-device summarization control: an Advanced setting lets you keep session summaries on your Mac, with Apple Intelligence handling longer sessions smoothly.
  • Faster Session Map: session reports build smoothly in the background without blocking the window.
  • More reliable layout sync: saved layouts apply cleanly across devices even when new accounts or hidden rows are discovered.

item.title: Tokematic 1.1.1206
item.description:
• Saved API keys and existing credential grants work again without enabling requests for new access.
  • Keychain and browser access requests share one checkbox. Safari remains separate because it needs Full Disk Access. Provider Settings offer web sign-in as an alternative.
  • The Keychain guide remembers when you continued, so restarting the app or changing the checkbox does not show it again.
  • Repeated login failures now show one error per known account. Sources that need the same fix share one clear notice with a link to provider Settings.
  • Claude refreshes again after access is granted, and blocked sources remain visible when no working source can provide a reading.
  • Codex no longer suggests a Business plan as an upgrade from a personal plan.

item.title: Tokematic 1.1.563
item.description:
• Check for Updates now offers any newer release, including interim builds. Automatic updates still follow the Early Access Updates checkbox.
  • Browser, Safari and Claude CLI Keychain support now require an explicit opt-in. Older automatic settings do not count as consent, so you may need to enable these options again in Settings.
  • Browser scans share one Keychain read per item during each app session, reducing repeated access prompts after opt-in.
  • Preferences and Conversations now share the Glacier design, with clearer spacing, type and controls.
  • Updated conversation pricing for GPT-5.6 models.
  • Improved the Mac’s change notifications for synced iPhone widgets.

item.title: Tokematic 1.1.531
item.description:
• Conversations rows now carry the real vendor mark in brand colour, and tokens, cost and time sit in fixed right-aligned columns so the numbers line up from row to row.
  • Split token counts: the new In/Out toggle splits each conversation’s tokens into separate input and output columns, both sortable like the rest.
  • Column headers sit in a row of their own at the top of the list, always visible for sorting, and the filter chips show a clear ring when they are on.
  • The newest GPT-6 models are priced, so conversations on them show real costs instead of “unpriced”.
  • Fixed a pace figure that could spike impossibly high when a provider’s additional quota limit leaked into the weekly and five-hour histories.
  • The Conversations window recentres itself if it ever reopens off the edge of the screen.

item.title: Tokematic 1.1.519
item.description:
INTERIM RELEASE - LAST 1.0 BEFORE BIG CHANGES

We’ve picked up a lot of menu options and sync confusion. This is a release to get a lot of important bug fixes before we turn back to some bigger things. As usual, let us know about any bugs but expect another release real soon now.

  • New provider: z.ai (GLM Coding Plan) joins the list, with its own Preferences tab, plan ladder, vendor mark and a model-by-model usage ledger. Sign-in details are picked up from the Zcode CLI config when they are already on your Mac.
  • Sign in from inside the app: subscription providers now open an in-app web sign-in, so you no longer have to fish session tokens out of a browser.
  • Preferences has a new look: every pane is rebuilt on shared cards, toggles, buttons and tip chips, with bundled MiSans and JetBrains Mono type and windows sized to the design.
  • Conversations shows the whole tree: subagent runs nest under the session that spawned them and sessions fired from one brief fold into a single wave row. Each row now carries a short local name and a separate shareable one.
  • Conversations also gains sortable columns, a date range, durations, smarter digests, the repo origin and commit for each session and an Obfuscate switch that strips names from the list. Automated pings fold away and long titles wrap.
  • Kimi’s monthly membership pool shows as its own quota row, the desktop app’s token store is read directly and the account-region setting is honoured for both Kimi and z.ai.
  • Pace follows where you work: Tokematic learns your work pattern per place, so a quiet week at home no longer reads as falling behind.
  • Codex quota readings key on each window’s real length, so the five-hour and weekly windows keep separate pace histories after the migration.
  • Clock times use your own locale’s spelling, a week means seven calendar days and the edit-mode window matches the resting window’s gaps and type.
  • Privacy: usage harvesting never reads a working directory that sits behind a macOS privacy prompt.
  • Sync: replay lets the newest client win, and the iCloud rail is checked record by record before any migration cuts over. Sealed sync now has full parity on iCloud and the Return to iCloud offer copies, verifies and cuts over in one step.
  • Saved views: arrange the Mac window once and publish that layout to your iPhone.
  • Window rows resize smoothly under pressure instead of clipping the chrome, and the Conversations summary holds its content height.

item.title: Tokematic 1.1.389
item.description:
• Arrange the window the way you want it: the window is now its own layout, so you can drag readings and headings into place, tick exactly which readings each account shows and rename them in place. Command-Z undoes any change.
  • Group your accounts in the window, shade each group by its vendor colour and fold a group shut when you want it out of the way. A vendor you sum keeps one full header however many accounts feed it.
  • See what you are actually running: the new Conversations view lists your live sessions, each named by what it was about.
  • Pace is an ordinary reading now, one per quota window, with four plain-language bands so you can tell at a glance whether you are ahead or behind.
  • The menu bar and the window each keep their own arrangement, so you can lay them out differently. Option-drag to move things and the changes carry across your devices.
  • New Apple-only sync: your iPhone reads your usage straight from your own iCloud, with nothing handed to us. The private iCloud store holds no readable data either way.
  • Watch overflow spending build: the spend row and its menu bar tooltip show a per-day rate and what a week at that pace projects. A new alert warns you before extra usage runs away.
  • Choose how hot readings stand out: a Colour or Monochrome switch on the Display tab tints the meters or keeps the older italic-then-bold look for them.
  • Kimi billing reads true: the booster wallet shows as Extra Usage and the pay-as-you-go API balance shows as Credits. A hand-linked key no longer folds onto the subscription and double-counts.
  • Check for Updates and Early Access Updates moved to the About tab, beside the version they act on.
  • Adding an API key no longer crashes and Return commits it. Renaming a key holds focus and saves when you click away.

item.title: Tokematic 1.0.215
item.description:
• Pick a colour per provider from a new grouped palette (choices that work in both appearances, plus brighter dark-only and light-only sets) and choose where it shows: menu bar controls, or each provider's section background and title band in the window.
  • A vendor you sum now draws one combined slot in the menu bar, instead of repeating the same total once per account.
  • Named API keys show their name everywhere instead of the last four characters, and each linked account says whether it is a subscription or an API key.
  • Renaming an API key no longer fights you: Return commits, Escape cancels and clicking away keeps the edit.
  • No more false "sign in to iCloud": sync only says that when you are genuinely signed out, and recovers by itself from momentary hiccups.
  • Reset times render properly on 24-hour clocks ("Resets today 1700", not "Resets today 17").
  • Fixed a crash when opening the Sync tab.
  • Preferences fits its content exactly: the Alerts grid keeps its margins, About drops the old Pro entry and the menu bar preview now matches your real menu bar.

item.title: Tokematic 1.0.121
item.description:
• Choose how often you hear about updates: major and minor releases are always offered, and the new Fast track updates switch in Preferences opts you into every interim build.
  • Get a clear alert when Tokematic is missing Full Disk Access, with a one-tap restart the moment you grant it, so usage numbers start flowing without a trip to System Settings.
  • Stale readings now fade in the menu bar and in each row, so you can tell at a glance when a number is old rather than current.
  • Short-lived sign-in hiccups no longer blank your usage: the last good reading stays on screen while the connection recovers.
  • Sign in with your existing local Claude credentials and let Tokematic keep the session refreshed on its own, so you stop getting logged out.
  • Track several accounts at once, each with its own menu-bar section, and pick exactly which ones show up.
  • Usage keeps updating while Tokematic sits in the background, so the figures are fresh the moment you open the menu.
  • New optional cloud sync plus a web dashboard, for checking your usage away from your Mac.
  • When a Keychain read fails, the message says why, and the About panel now shows the full version and build.

item.title: Tokematic 1.0.88
item.description:
• Multiple accounts with the same vendor collapse into one summed row — and the combined total shows in the menu bar itself, not just the dropdown.
  • The same login signed in from several places folds into a single row, matched by email — no more seeing the same account three times.
  • When a login is visible from more than one source, the most reliable one stands for it. Command-line sessions win over browser sessions.
  • Sessions Tokematic can't read are hidden whenever a working source already covers that login — dead entries stop cluttering the list.
  • Money alerts name the actual problem: Payment issue, Out of credits, Low balance.
  • Fewer bogus out-of-credits warnings — the alert only fires when a recently-funded balance really runs down.
  • Past-due detection catches cases it used to miss.
  • API keys can be associated with an account, and the key list no longer shows other vendors' keys.
  • New Hide control for accounts you'd rather not watch.
  • Account links you make by hand stick across refreshes and restarts; learned account identities are remembered, so sessions re-attach on their own.
  • Every browser profile is checked now, not just the default one.
  • Preferences buttons are now compact glyphs; Unlink only appears where it applies.
  • Version shows as marketing version plus build; dist builds are signed; settings sync over iCloud.
